title: Prompt Injection Alert to the Security Team
dataSources: Luna Prompt Injection scores on sampled traces, counted by the stream alert
description: Notifies the security team when Luna Prompt Injection flags traces on an Agent Stream, using a count alert on the evaluator with a Slack or generic HTTP webhook notification.
value: A burst of injection attempts can mean an active attack or a poisoned document in retrieval. The alert brings in security quickly, with a deep link to the traces.
implementation: On the Agent Stream's Alerts tab, add a count alert on Luna Prompt Injection with a threshold and window agreed with security, and notify the security channel by Slack incoming webhook or generic HTTP webhook.
visualization: Alerts tab history; deep link from the notification to the flagged traces.
knownFalsePositives: Red-team exercises trigger it. Run them on a separate stream. A count alert on an evaluator counts sampled traces only, so the real number of attempts can be higher at sample rates below 100%.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The agent is already instrumented as described in UC-13.8.1: every request is a trace with at least one agent span, LLM spans carry `model`, token counts and the `tools` schemas, and tool spans carry `name`, `duration_ns` and `tool_call_id`.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open the Agent Stream, go to the Alerts tab and add an alert. Each alert is an evaluator or a built-in metric (Status Code, Cost, Latency, Trace Count), an aggregation (average, min, max, count or sum), a threshold and a window. Notifications go to email, a Slack incoming webhook or a generic HTTP webhook. Alerts never block a request. A generic HTTP webhook receives a body with `event` (`alert.triggered`), `conditions[].observed_value`, `dedup_key`, `deep_link` and any `metadata` configured on the webhook. Webhook auth is none, bearer or HTTP basic, and the credential is write-only after save.

Step 3 — Validate

Send a known injection string to a test stream at a 100% sample rate and confirm the notification. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Agree the response with security: who reviews the traces, and when an inline control (UC-13.8.26) is added. Forwarding the webhook into the Splunk platform is not covered here; it needs a tested webhook-to-HEC path first.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No notification: check webhook auth (none, bearer or HTTP basic); the credential is write-only after save, so re-enter it if unsure.
grandmaExplanation: When the guard sees people trying to trick the assistant, the security team gets a message straight away.

productArtifacts.title: Prompt injection count alert
productArtifacts.body:
Where: Agent Stream > Alerts tab > add alert
Metric: Luna Prompt Injection (evaluator enabled on the stream)
Aggregation: count
Condition: Count of flagged traces at or above the agreed number for the window
Window: match the team's response time; a shorter window alerts sooner and is noisier
Notification: email, Slack incoming webhook, or generic HTTP webhook
Notes: Counts sampled traces only. The webhook body carries dedup_key and deep_link for the security team's tooling.
